now.v: Synapse, a local-first memory for agents. It only cares about two numbers: speed and cost.
Synapse against LongMemEval. Vibes are not a metric.
Lunch & learns at work on Claude: memory, artifacts, video. The goal is for the whole company to show up.
Weird web behavior, for a talk. I’d rather build a tiny broken version than read another tutorial.

chapters.b: The first thing people actually used was a Go tool that pulls 20,000+ V2Ray configs, dedupes them and rebuilds the list every 6 hours. A run takes 11 seconds. It has 155 stars now, which is wild. That’s when speed became my whole personality.

Next I got into networks that don’t want to be mapped. I wrote a scanner that pokes Cloudflare and Fastly edges and flags DPI tricks and MITM, then built a live dashboard that tracks internet shutdowns in Iran. Some code matters more than the rest.
December 2025: I graduated from Computer Programming at Algonquin College. My curiosity didn’t. It got worse.
Then I noticed AI agents forget everything, and it felt like a bug in the universe. Now most of my days go to memory systems, local-first stuff and open source. No regrets. Mostly.

loves.b: Your data. Your disk. If it needs someone else’s server to remember your name, you’re renting it.
No benchmark? Then it’s a guess. I learned that the hard way, and it’s in my writing.
Runtimes, compilers, networking, databases, Unicode and RTL text. The “wait, why does it do that?” stuff.
Reading other people’s code is the fastest way to get humbled. I love it.

projects.name: synapse
projects.story: A local-first memory system for AI agents: write memory in, embed it locally, answer by retrieval. The hard part is getting agents to check memory before they reply. Rules files are just suggestions, so Synapse uses tool_choice and hooks instead.

projects.name: v2go
projects.story: Grabs 20,000+ V2Ray configs, dedupes them and rebuilds the list every 6 hours. 11 seconds a run. Go was the right call.

projects.name: cf-knife
projects.story: A pocket knife for networks that hate being mapped. It probes Cloudflare and Fastly edges over TLS and HTTP and flags DPI tricks and MITM.

projects.name: iran-internet-monitor
projects.story: A live dashboard tracking connectivity and censorship in Iran. When the internet goes dark, somebody should be counting.

projects.name: llm-map
projects.story: Every AI language model on one interactive 3D chart. Compare smartness, cost, speed and ARC-AGI-2 scores, filter by date, and step inside the chart. English and Persian.

projects.name: syncodoro
projects.story: A Pomodoro timer that works offline and syncs when you’re back online. It shows stats too, so you can see how locked in you really were. Usually less than you think.

projects.name: free-macos
projects.story: macOS never shipped Linux’s free command, so now it does. Live memory stats, right in your terminal.

projects.name: netray
projects.story: Network diagnostics in Go. Small, sharp, no fluff.

experience.b: Memory tools that agents check before every answer, even when they’d rather not.
Shipping at work. I also run company-wide lunch & learns on Claude.
Go tools, network scanners, PWAs. Lately, AI memory and LLM tooling.
Graduated, then kept building way past the assignment.

title: boo. i’m dani.
i give ai agents a memory.
body: Every AI agent you’ve used forgets you the second the tab closes. Every. Single. One.
That bugs me way more than it should. So I’m building them a memory that lives on your laptop, not in a data center. Open source, local-first, and still a little broken. Getting there.
